commentaries.whitney: Triply born by birth [is] this gold: one was Agni's dearest; one fell away of Soma when injured; one they call the seed of devout waters; let that triple gold be thine in order to life-time.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Instead of vedhásām in d , a much easier reading would be vedhásas nom. (as tacitlyemended by Ludwig); and this is favored by Ppp., which has vedaso retā ”hus; it further gives in e trivṛtāstu te . With bcd compare TB. i. 1. 3 8 . The name atiçakvarī given to the verse by the Anukr. demands 60 syllables, but only 57 (11 + 11 + 12: 11 + 12) can be fairly counted.

commentaries.whitney: Triple life-time of Jamadagni, Kaçyapa's triple life-time, sight of the immortal ( amṛ́ta ) triply, three life-times have I made for thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads triyāyuṣam; and, at the end, nas kṛdhi for te ‘karam . JUB. iv. 3. 1 has this version: triyāyuṣaṁ kaçyapasya jamadagnes triyāyuṣam: trīṇy amṛtasya puṣpāṇi trīṇ āyūṅṣi me ‘kṛṇoḥ; and several of the Gṛhya-Sūtras (ÇGS. i. 28; HGS. i. 9. 6; ⌊MP. ii. 7. 2; MGS. i. 1. 24 (cf. p. 150)⌋; MB. i. 6. 8) give the first half-verse, with a different ending; ⌊also VS. iii. 62. GGS. ii. 9. 21 gives the pratīka .⌋ There is no reason for calling the meter kakummatī .

commentaries.whitney: When the three eagles ( suparṇá ) went with the triple one, becoming, mighty ones ( çakrá ), a single syllable, they bore back death along with ( sākám ) the immortal, warding off ( antar-dhā ) all difficulties.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Warding off,' literally 'interposing [something between] themselves [and]'; 'along with,' doubtless = 'by means of' (cf. vii. 53. 1: xii. 2. 29). 'Single syllable,' or 'the one indissoluble': probably the syllable om is intended.

items.samhita_patha_plain: त्रयः सुपर्णास्त्रिवृता यदायन्नेकाक्षरमभिसंभूय शक्राः। प्रत्यौहन्मृत्युममृतेन साकमन्तर्दधाना दुरितानि विश्वा ॥

items.samhita_patha: दि॒वस्त्वा॑ पातु॒ हरि॑तं॒ मध्या॑त्त्वा पा॒त्वर्जु॑नम्। भूम्या॑ अय॒स्मयं॑ पातु॒ प्रागा॑द्देवपु॒रा अ॒यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: From the sky let the yellow one protect thee; from the midst let the silver one protect thee; from the earth let that made of iron protect [thee]; this [man] hath gone forward to strongholds of the gods.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines at the end -purā ’yam . This verse also is called kakummatī by the Anukr. without any reason.

items.samhita_patha_plain: दिवस्त्वा पातु हरितं मध्यात्त्वा पात्वर्जुनम्। भूम्या अयस्मयं पातु प्रागाद्देवपुरा अयम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: इ॒मास्ति॒स्रो दे॑वपु॒रास्तास्त्वा॑ रक्षन्तु स॒र्वतः॑। तास्त्वं बिभ्र॑द्वर्च॒स्व्युत्त॑रो द्विष॒तां भ॑व ॥

commentaries.whitney: These [are] three strongholds of the gods; let them defend thee on all sides; bearing these, do thou, possessing splendor, become superior to them that hate thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: It needs only the usual resolution tu-ám in c to make this verse a regular anuṣṭubh .

items.samhita_patha_plain: इमास्तिस्रो देवपुरास्तास्त्वा रक्षन्तु सर्वतः। तास्त्वं बिभ्रद्वर्चस्व्युत्तरो द्विषतां भव ॥

items.samhita_patha: पुरं॑ दे॒वाना॑म॒मृतं॒ हिर॑ण्यं॒ य आ॑बे॒धे प्र॑थ॒मो दे॒वो अग्रे॑। तस्मै॒ नमो॒ दश॒ प्राचीः॑ कृणो॒म्यनु॑ मन्यतां त्रि॒वृदा॒बधे॑ मे ॥

commentaries.whitney: The stronghold of the gods, deathless ( amṛ́ta ) gold, what god first bound on in the beginning, to him I pay homage, [my] ten extended [fingers]; let him approve my binding-on the triple one.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has at the end trivṛtā vadhena . The translation implies in d the reading manyatām , which is given in our edition, though against part of the mss., that read manyantām . ⌊'Let him (or it) assent to my binding-on,' dative infinitive.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: पुरं देवानाममृतं हिरण्यं य आबेधे प्रथमो देवो अग्रे। तस्मै नमो दश प्राचीः कृणोम्यनु मन्यतां त्रिवृदाबधे मे ॥

items.samhita_patha: आ त्वा॑ चृतत्वर्य॒मा पू॒षा बृह॒स्पतिः॑। अह॑र्जातस्य॒ यन्नाम॒ तेन॒ त्वाति॑ चृतामसि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let Aryaman fasten ( cṛt ) thee on, let Pūshan, let Brihaspati; what is the name of the day-born one, therewith we fasten thee over.
commentaries.whitney_notes: For the obscure third pāda compare iii. 14. 1. The verse is a regular anuṣṭubh , if b is properly read, as ā́ pūṣā́ ā́ bṛ́haspátiḥ (so the pada -text). This and the two following verses, which are not found in Ppp., seem to be independent of what precedes.

items.samhita_patha: ऋ॒तुभि॑ष्ट्वार्त॒वैरायु॑षे॒ वर्च॑से त्वा। सं॑वत्स॒रस्य॒ तेज॑सा॒ तेन॒ संह॑नु कृण्मसि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thee with the seasons, with them of the seasons; thee unto lifetime, unto splendor; with the brilliancy of the year—with that we make [thee] of closed jaw (? sáṁhanu ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse is repeated as xix. 37.4 ⌊in our ed.; but SPP's repeats iii. 10. 10 instead⌋. It is found also in HGS. i. 11. 2, with tvā omitted at the end of b , and, for c, d , saṁvatsarasya dhāyasā tena sann anu gṛhṇāsi! this gives us no help toward understanding the obscure last pāda; the translation implies emendation to sáṁhanum , and understands the verse as directed against involuntary opening of the jaws ( divaricatio maxillae inferioris ): cf. viii. 1. 16. The Anukr. foolishly calls the verse a purauṣṇih .

commentaries.whitney: Snatched ( lup ) out of ghee, anointed over with honey, fixing the earth, unmoved, rescuing, splitting [our] rivals, and putting them down, do thou ascend me in order to great good-fortune.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse agrees nearly with xix. 33. 2. The mss. read bhindánt (p. bhindán ) for bhindát in c . A corresponding verse is found in a RV. khila to x. 128: ghṛtād ulluptam madhumat suvarṇaṁ dhanaṁjayaṁ dharuṇaṁ dhārayiṣṇu: ṛṇak sapatnān adharāṅç ca kṛṇvad ā roha mām mahate sāubhagāya . ⌊Given also by von Schroeder, Tübinger Kaṭha-hss. , p. 36.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Joined in front, carry thou, O Jātavedas; know this, O Agni, as [it is] being done; thou art a physician ( bhiṣáj ), a maker of remedy ( bheṣajá ); by thee may we gain cow, horse, man ( púruṣa ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is ( b ), take notice of this rite performed in thine honor. The verse is found also in HGS. i. 2. 18, which in a puts (as does Ppp.) purastāt at the end, inserts in b karma after viddhi , and reads in d gā açvān puruṣān . Kāuç. (3. 16) quotes the verse, in company with several others, at a certain libation in the parvan ceremonies.

items.samhita_patha: तथा॒ तद॑ग्ने कृणु जातवेदो॒ विश्वे॑भिर्दे॒वैः स॒ह सं॑विदा॒नः। यो नो॑ दि॒देव॑ यत॒मो ज॒घास॒ यथा॒ सो अ॒स्य प॑रि॒धिष्पता॑ति ॥

commentaries.whitney: So, O Agni, Jātavedas, do thou do this, in concord with all the gods: he who hath played [against] us, whosoever hath devoured ( ghas ) us, that this enclosure of his may fall.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The sense of c appears to be 'whoever hath pillaged us in or by play.' The sense of the imprecation in d is obscure. Ppp. reads as follows: tvam for tat in a ; for b, c ’nena vidvān haviṣā yaviṣṭhaḥ: piçāco ‘syatamo* dideva; ‘sya in d ; and, as e (or as 3 a ), yo ‘sya tad eva yatamo jaghāsi . Kāuç. 47. 9 quotes the verse (the scholiast says, vss. 2, 3) as accompanying the offering of portions of sacrificial butter in witchcraft ceremonies. The Prāt., in ii. 77, prescribes the combination -dhíṣ pát- in d . *⌊Haplography for ‘sya yatamo: cf. 4 c .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: तथा तदग्ने कृणु जातवेदो विश्वेभिर्देवैः सह संविदानः। यो नो दिदेव यतमो जघास यथा सो अस्य परिधिष्पताति ॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒क्ष्यौ॒ नि वि॑ध्य॒ हृद॑यं॒ नि वि॑ध्य जि॒ह्वां नि तृ॑न्द्धि॒ प्र द॒तो मृ॑णीहि। पि॑शा॒चो अ॒स्य य॑त॒मो ज॒घासाग्ने॑ यविष्ठ॒ प्रति॑ तं शृणीहि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Pierce thou into his eyes, pierce into his heart, bore into his tongue, destroy ( pra-mṛ ) his teeth; whatsoever piçācá hath devoured of him, that one, O Agni, youngest [god], do thou crush back.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads for a mokṣāu na viddhi hṛdayaṁ na viddhi and piçāco syatamo in c , and yaviṣṭhaṣ in d . Kāuç. (25. 24) quotes the verse in a remedial ceremony.

commentaries.whitney: What of him is taken [or] taken apart, what is borne away, whatsoever of himself is devoured by the piçācás , that, O Agni, do thou, knowing, bring again; into his body we send flesh [and] spirit ( ásu ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads for d çarīre prāṇam asum erayā saṁ sṛjema . The Anukr. defines the meter correctly, according to its methods.

commentaries.whitney: In raw, in well-cooked, in mixed (? çabála ), in ripe, what piçācá hath injured ( dambh ) me in the partaking—that let the piçācás atone for (? vi-yātay ) with self [and] progeny; be this man free from disease.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has for a our 8 a (reading tvā for mā ), and for 8 a yāme sap. çavale vip.; further, for b odane manthe diva ota lehe; and here and in the verses that follow, it varies between dadambha and didambha .

commentaries.whitney_notes: We are tempted to emend (with Ludwig) çáyānam to çáyānas at end of b . Ppp. reads here, in a, b , nearly our 6 a, b, a with the three variants given above, and b with imam for yo mā , and with ‘çane; and it adds our 10 c, d instead of the refrain.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads tvā for mā in a , and in b ṣkravyād yātuç çayate piçācaḥ: ud agne dvān pṛthak: çṛṇīhy apy enaṁ dehi nirṛter upasthe . In c of the refrain of all these verses is a syllable lacking, unless we make a harsh and unusual resolution.

items.samhita_patha: क्र॒व्याद॑मग्ने रुधि॒रं पि॑शा॒चं म॑नो॒हनं॑ जहि जातवेदः। तमिन्द्रो॑ वा॒जी वज्रे॑ण हन्तु छि॒नत्तु॒ सोमः॒ शिरो॑ अस्य धृ॒ष्णुः ॥

commentaries.whitney: The flesh-eating, bloody ( rudhirá ), mind-slaying piçācá do thou slay, O Agni, Jātavedas; let the vigorous Indra slay him with the thunderbolt; let bold Soma cut [off] his head.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. takes no notice of the lacking syllables in b and c , the latter of which, indeed, is easily made up for by resolving vá-jṛ-e-ṇa .

items.samhita_patha_plain: क्रव्यादमग्ने रुधिरं पिशाचं मनोहनं जहि जातवेदः। तमिन्द्रो वाजी वज्रेण हन्तु छिनत्तु सोमः शिरो अस्य धृष्णुः ॥

items.samhita_patha: स॒नाद॑ग्ने मृणसि यातु॒धाना॒न्न त्वा॒ रक्षां॑सि॒ पृत॑नासु जिग्युः। स॒हमू॑रा॒ननु॑ दह क्र॒व्यादो॒ मा ते॑ हे॒त्या मु॑क्षत॒ दैव्या॑याः ॥

commentaries.whitney: From of old, O Agni, thou killest the sorcerers; the demons have not conquered thee in fights; burn up the flesh-eaters together with their dupes (?); let them not be freed from thy heavenly missile.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse is repeated below as viii. 3. 18, in the midst of the RV. hymn of which it forms a part: see the note upon it there.

items.samhita_patha_plain: सनादग्ने मृणसि यातुधानान्न त्वा रक्षांसि पृतनासु जिग्युः। सहमूराननु दह क्रव्यादो मा ते हेत्या मुक्षत दैव्यायाः ॥

items.samhita_patha: स॒माह॑र जातवेदो॒ यद्धृ॒तं यत्परा॑भृतम्। गात्रा॑ण्यस्य वर्धन्तामं॒शुरि॒वा प्या॑यताम॒यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Bring together, O Jātavedas, what is taken, what borne away; let his members ( gā́tra ) increase; let this man fill up like a soma-stalk.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. begins with samābhara , and has jagdham for hṛtam in b . The Anukr. refuses to sanction the abbreviation ’va in d .

items.samhita_patha_plain: समाहर जातवेदो यद्धृतं यत्पराभृतम्। गात्राण्यस्य वर्धन्तामंशुरिवा प्यायतामयम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: सोम॑स्येव जातवेदो अं॒शुरा प्या॑यताम॒यम्। अग्ने॑ विर॒प्शिनं॒ मेध्य॑मय॒क्ष्मं कृ॑णु॒ जीव॑तु ॥

commentaries.whitney: Like a stalk of soma, O Jātavedas, let this man fill up; make him, O Agni, exuberant, sacrificial ( médhya ), free from yákṣma; let him live.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. is illegible in the last half of the preceding verse and the first of this; it reads at the end jīvase . Our mss. are uncertain about virapçínam , B.E.H. having -psí- , I. -ptrā́- , O. -çpí .

items.samhita_patha_plain: सोमस्येव जातवेदो अंशुरा प्यायतामयम्। अग्ने विरप्शिनं मेध्यमयक्ष्मं कृणु जीवतु ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: सोमस्यऽइव । जातऽवेद: । अशु: । आ । प्यायताम् । अयम् । अग्ने । विऽरप्शिनम् । मेध्यम् । अयक्ष्मम् । कृणु । जीवतु ॥२९.१३॥

items.samhita_patha: ए॒तास्ते॑ अग्ने स॒मिधः॑ पिशाच॒जम्भ॑नीः। तास्त्वं जु॑षस्व॒ प्रति॑ चैना गृहाण जातवेदः ॥

commentaries.whitney: These, O Agni, are thy piçācá -grinding pieces of fuel; them do thou enjoy, and accept them, O Jātavedas.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The irregular and defective meter of this verse is very inaccurately described by the Anukr.; it counts as 8 + 6: 5 + 11 syllables, having thus a kakubh -element ( b ), but no bṛhatī .

items.samhita_patha_plain: एतास्ते अग्ने समिधः पिशाचजम्भनीः। तास्त्वं जुषस्व प्रति चैना गृहाण जातवेदः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: एता: । ते । अग्ने । सम्ऽइध: । पिशाचऽजम्भनी: । ता: । त्वम् । जुषस्व । प्रति । च । एना: । गृहाण । जातऽवेद: ॥२९.१४॥

items.samhita_patha: ता॑र्ष्टा॒घीर॑ग्ने स॒मिधः॒ प्रति॑ गृह्णाह्य॒र्चिषा॑। जहा॑तु क्र॒व्याद्रू॒पं यो अ॑स्य मां॒सं जिही॑र्षति ॥
items.pada_patha: ता॒र्ष्ट॒ऽअ॒घी: । अ॒ग्ने॒ । स॒म्ऽइध॑: । प्रति॑ । गृ॒ह्णा॒हि॒ । अ॒र्चिषा॑ । जहा॑तु । क्र॒व्य॒ऽअत् । रू॒पम् । य: । अ॒स्य॒ । मां॒सम् । जिही॑र्षति ॥२९.१५॥

commentaries.whitney:
The pieces of fuel of tārṣṭāghá , O Agni, do thou accept with flame
( arcís ); let the flesh-eater who wants to take this man's flesh ( māṅsá ) quit his form.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or 'of tṛṣṭāgha ' ( a ); this name, however, seems not to be met with anywhere; the pada -text reads tārṣṭa॰aghī́h .

items.samhita_patha_plain: तार्ष्टाघीरग्ने समिधः प्रति गृह्णाह्यर्चिषा। जहातु क्रव्याद्रूपं यो अस्य मांसं जिहीर्षति ॥

items.samhita_patha: आ॒वत॑स्त आ॒वतः॑ परा॒वत॑स्त आ॒वतः॑। इ॒हैव भ॑व॒ मा नु गा॒ मा पूर्वा॒ननु॑ गाः पि॒तॄनसुं॑ बध्नामि ते दृ॒ढम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thy nearnesses [are] nearnesses, thy distances nearnesses; be just here; go not now; go not after the former Fathers; thy life ( ásu ) I bind fast.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first two pādas are obscure; the two nouns in each can also be both or either ablatives (so Muir) or genitives sing. Ppp. reads parāvatas instead of the second āvatas , thus rectifying the meter of a ; as it stands, we need to resolve a-āvátas ⌊or read táva for te .⌋ Ppp. also has gatān for pitṝn in d .

items.samhita_patha_plain: आवतस्त आवतः परावतस्त आवतः। इहैव भव मा नु गा मा पूर्वाननु गाः पितॄनसुं बध्नामि ते दृढम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: यत्त्वा॑भिचे॒रुः पुरु॑षः॒ स्वो यदर॑णो॒ जनः॑। उ॑न्मोचनप्रमोच॒ने उ॒भे वा॒चा व॑दामि ते ॥

commentaries.whitney: In that men have bewitched thee, one of thine own people [or] a strange person—deliverance and release, both I speak for thee with my voice.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies emendation to púruṣās in a ; all the mss. have -ṣas . ⌊SPP's texts have -ṣas without note of variant. We may construe it with the second yát: 'If they (subject indef.) have bewitched thee, if a man of thine own' etc.—supply abhicacā́ra ⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यत्त्वाभिचेरुः पुरुषः स्वो यदरणो जनः। उन्मोचनप्रमोचने उभे वाचा वदामि ते ॥

items.samhita_patha: यद्दु॒द्रोहि॑थ शेपि॒षे स्त्रि॒यै पुं॒से अचि॑त्त्या। उ॑न्मोचनप्रमोच॒ने उ॒भे वा॒चा व॑दामि ते ॥
items.pada_patha: यत् । दु॒द्रोहि॑थ । शे॒पि॒षे । स्त्रि॒यै । पु॒से । अचि॑त्त्या । उ॒न्मो॒च॒न॒प्र॒मो॒च॒ने इत्यु॑न्मोचनऽप्रमोच॒ने । उ॒भे इति॑ । वा॒चा । व॒दा॒मि॒ । ते॒ ॥३०.३॥

commentaries.whitney: In that thou hast shown malice ( druh ), hast cursed at woman [or] at man through thoughtlessness, deliverance and etc. etc.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यद्दुद्रोहिथ शेपिषे स्त्रियै पुंसे अचित्त्या। उन्मोचनप्रमोचने उभे वाचा वदामि ते ॥

items.samhita_patha: यदेन॑सो मा॒तृकृ॑ता॒च्छेषे॑ पि॒तृकृ॑ताच्च॒ यत्। उ॑न्मोचनप्रमोच॒ने उ॒भे वा॒चा व॑दामि ते ॥

commentaries.whitney: In that thou art prostrate ( çī ) from sin that is mother-committed and that is father-committed, deliverance and etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Grohmann and Zimmer (p. 395) understand here 'sin committed against mother or father': doubtless wrong.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदेनसो मातृकृताच्छेषे पितृकृताच्च यत्। उन्मोचनप्रमोचने उभे वाचा वदामि ते ॥

items.samhita_patha: यत्ते॑ मा॒ता यत्ते॑ पि॒ता जा॒मिर्भ्राता॑ च॒ सर्ज॑तः। प्र॒त्यक्से॑वस्व भेष॒जं ज॒रद॑ष्टिं कृणोमि त्वा ॥

commentaries.whitney: What thy mother, what thy father, sister ( jāmí ), and brother shall infuse (? sárjatas )—heed ( sev ) thou the opposing remedy; I make thee one who reaches old age.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Sárjatas is a puzzle, as regards both form and sense; 'give ' (Ludwig) and 'offer' (Muir) are wholly unsatisfactory; 'weave witchcraft' (Pet. Lex.) is quite too pregnant. Ppp. gives no help; it reads in c chevasya after pratyak . The translation takes the word as a root-aorist subj. from sṛj .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यत्ते माता यत्ते पिता जामिर्भ्राता च सर्जतः। प्रत्यक्सेवस्व भेषजं जरदष्टिं कृणोमि त्वा ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यत् । ते । माता । यत् । ते । पिता । जामि: । भ्राता । च । सर्जत: । प्रत्यक् । सेवस्व । भेषजम् । जरत्ऽअष्टिम् । कृणोमि। त्वा ॥३०.५॥

items.samhita_patha: इ॒हैधि॑ पुरुष॒ सर्वे॑ण॒ मन॑सा स॒ह। दू॒तौ य॒मस्य॒ मानु॑ गा॒ अधि॑ जीवपु॒रा इ॑हि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Be thou here, O man, together with thy whole mind; go not after Yama's (two) messengers; go unto the strongholds of the living.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. takes no notice of the defective first pāda; the addition of evá (cf. 1 c ) after ihá would be an easy and natural filling-out. Ppp. has for a ehi ehi punar ehi , and reads hi for ihi in d .

commentaries.whitney: Being called after, come thou again, knowing the up-going of the road, the ascent, the climb ( ākrámaṇa ), the course ( áyana ) of every living man.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads for b jaradaṣṭir bhaviṣyasi .

commentaries.whitney: The splitter of limbs, the waster of limbs, and the heart-ache that is thine, the yákṣma hath flown forth like a falcon, forced ( sah ) very far away by [my] voice.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The form sāḍhá is noted in Prāt. iii. 7. Ppp. has for a çīrṣarogam an̄garogam , combines çyenāi ’va in c , and reads nuttas for sāḍhas in d ⌊and vācā? ⌋. The Anukr. ignores the abbreviation of iva to ’va in c .

items.samhita_patha: ऋषी॑ बोधप्रतीबो॒धाव॑स्व॒प्नो यश्च॒ जागृ॑विः। तौ ते॑ प्रा॒णस्य॑ गो॒प्तारौ॒ दिवा॒ नक्तं॑ च जागृताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: The two seers, Wakeful-and- Vigilant, sleepless and he that is watchful—let them, the guardians of thy breath, watch by day and by night.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for c, d , te te prāṇasya goptaro divā svapnaṁ ca jāgratu . Pada -text bodha॰pratībodhā́u , by Prāt. iv. 96. ⌊Cf. viii. i. 13; MGS. ii. 15. 1 and p. 153, s.v. bodha- .⌋

items.samhita_patha: अ॒यम॒ग्निरु॑प॒सद्य॑ इ॒ह सूर्य॒ उदे॑तु ते। उ॒देहि॑ मृ॒त्योर्ग॑म्भी॒रात्कृ॒ष्णाच्चि॒त्तम॑स॒स्परि॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: This Agni [is] to be waited on; here let the sun arise for thee; come up out of death's profound black darkness.
commentaries.whitney_notes: In c , údehi is a mis-reading for udéhi , which is found in all the mss. except Bp. 2

commentaries.whitney: Homage to Yama, homage be to Death; homage to the Fathers, and [to them] who conduct [away]; that Agni who understands ( vid ) deliverance ( utpáraṇa ) do I put forward ( puro-dhā ), in order to this man's being unharmed.
commentaries.whitney_notes: With b compare viii. i. 8 b , which appears to give the clew to the meaning; utpāraṇa is the action-noun to ut-pāray (viii. 1. 17-19; 2. 9). The verse, though by number of syllables a virāḍ jagatī (46 syll.), has plainly five pādas ⌊12 + 11: 8 + 7 + 8; in d , read táṁ-tam for tám as at iv. 30. 3?⌋. Ppp. omits the last pāda.

items.samhita_patha: ऐतु॑ प्रा॒ण ऐतु॒ मन॒ ऐतु॒ चक्षु॒रथो॒ बल॑म्। शरी॑रमस्य॒ सम्वि॑दां॒ तत्प॒द्भ्यां प्रति॑ तिष्ठतु ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let breath come, let mind come, let sight come, then strength; let his body assemble (? sam-vid ); let that stand firm with its (two) feet.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊In a, b , the order of the items of the return to life is (if inverted) in noteworthy accord with that of the items of the process of death, both in fact and also as set forth in the Upanishads—e.g. ChU. vi. 15.⌋

commentaries.whitney: With breath, O Agni, with sight unite him; associate ( sam-īray ) him with body, with strength; thou understandest immortality ( amṛ́ta ): let him not now go; let him not now become one housing in the earth.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Most of our mss. (not B.I.T.K.) appear to read tú instead of nú in d . Instead of nu gāt in c , Ppp. gives mṛta , and it has mo ṣu for mā nu in d : both are better readings.

items.samhita_patha: मा ते॑ प्रा॒ण उप॑ दस॒न्मो अ॑पा॒नोऽपि॑ धायि ते। सूर्य॒स्त्वाधि॑पतिर्मृ॒त्योरु॒दाय॑च्छतु र॒श्मिभिः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let not thy breath give out, nor let thine expiration be shut up; let the sun, the over-lord, hold thee up out of death by his rays.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads mā ’pāno in b , and -yachati in d .

items.samhita_patha_plain: मा ते प्राण उप दसन्मो अपानोऽपि धायि ते। सूर्यस्त्वाधिपतिर्मृत्योरुदायच्छतु रश्मिभिः ॥

items.samhita_patha: इ॒यम॒न्तर्व॑दति जि॒ह्वा ब॒द्धा प॑निष्प॒दा। त्वया॒ यक्ष्मं निर॑वोचं श॒तं रोपी॑श्च त॒क्मनः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: This much-quivering tongue, bound, speaks within; by it I have exorcised the yákṣma and the hundred pangs of the fever.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads for b, c ugrajihvā paṇiṣpadā tayā romaṁ nir ayāsaḥ: . Our edition reads tváyā , with all the mss., at the beginning of c , but it must of course be emended to táyā , as translated. The Anukr. takes no notice of the lacking syllable in a , which no resolution can supply. Paniṣpadā in b is prescribed by Prāt. iv. 96.

items.samhita_patha_plain: इयमन्तर्वदति जिह्वा बद्धा पनिष्पदा। त्वया यक्ष्मं निरवोचं शतं रोपीश्च तक्मनः ॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒यं लो॒कः प्रि॒यत॑मो दे॒वाना॒मप॑राजितः। यस्मै॒ त्वमि॒ह मृ॒त्यवे॑ दि॒ष्टः पु॑रुष जज्ञि॒षे। स च॒ त्वानु॑ ह्वयामसि॒ मा पु॒रा ज॒रसो॑ मृथाः ॥

commentaries.whitney: This [is] the dearest world of the gods, unconquered. Unto what death appointed, O man, thou wast born here, we and it call after thee: do not die before old age.
commentaries.whitney_notes: By one of the most absurd of the many blunders of the pada -text, we find puruṣa॰jajñiṣé in d treated by it as a compound. Ppp. reads, for c-e , tasmāi tvam iha jajñiṣé adṛṣṭaṣ puruṣa mṛtyave: tasmāi tvā ni hvayāmasi .

items.samhita_patha_plain: अयं लोकः प्रियतमो देवानामपराजितः। यस्मै त्वमिह मृत्यवे दिष्टः पुरुष जज्ञिषे। स च त्वानु ह्वयामसि मा पुरा जरसो मृथाः ॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुरा॒मे पात्रे॒ यां च॒क्रुर्मि॒श्रधा॑न्ये। आ॒मे मां॒से कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in a raw vessel, what they have made in one of mixed grains; in raw flesh what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, doubtless, 'back to its maker': cf. iv. 18. 4; and, for the whole verse, iv. 17. 4. The Anukr. makes no account of the redundant syllable in c .

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुः कृ॑क॒वाका॑व॒जे वा॒ यां कु॑री॒रिणि॑। अव्यां॑ ते कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in a cock, or what in a kurī́ra -wearing goat; in a ewe what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Geldner discusses kurī́ra 'horn,' Ved. Stud. i. 130.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते चक्रुः कृकवाकावजे वा यां कुरीरिणि। अव्यां ते कृत्यां यां चक्रुः पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुरेक॑शफे पशू॒नामु॑भ॒याद॑ति। ग॑र्द॒भे कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in the one-hoofed, in the one with teeth in both jaws, among cattle; in a donkey what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते चक्रुरेकशफे पशूनामुभयादति। गर्दभे कृत्यां यां चक्रुः पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुर॑मू॒लायां॑ वल॒गं वा॑ नरा॒च्याम्। क्षेत्रे॑ ते कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in a rootless [plant], or [what] secret spell (? valagá ) in a narācī́; in thy field what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text does not divide valagám .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते चक्रुरमूलायां वलगं वा नराच्याम्। क्षेत्रे ते कृत्यां यां चक्रुः पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: याम् । ते । चक्रु: । अमूलायाम् । वलगम् । वा । नराच्याम् । क्षेत्रे । ते । कृत्याम् । याम् । चक्रु: । पुन: । प्रति । हरामि । ताम् ॥३१.४ ॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुर्गार्ह॑पत्ये पूर्वा॒ग्नावु॒त दु॒श्चितः॑। शाला॑यां कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in the householder's fire, also, malevolent ( duçcít ), in the eastern fire; in the dwelling what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते चक्रुर्गार्हपत्ये पूर्वाग्नावुत दुश्चितः। शालायां कृत्यां यां चक्रुः पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: याम् । ते ।चक्रु: । गार्हऽपत्ये । पूर्वऽअग्नौ । उत । दु:ऽचित: । शालायाम् । कृत्याम् । याम् । चक्रु: । पुन: । प्रति । हरामि । ताम् ॥३१.५॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुः स॒भायां॒ यां च॒क्रुर॑धि॒देव॑ने। अ॒क्षेषु॑ कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in the assembly ( sabhá ), what they have made at the gambling-board; in the dice what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते चक्रुः सभायां यां चक्रुरधिदेवने। अक्षेषु कृत्यां यां चक्रुः पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: याम् । ते । चक्रु: । सभायाम् । याम् । चक्रु: । अधिऽदेवने । अक्षेषु । कृत्याम् । याम् । चक्रु: । पुन: । प्रति । हरामि । ताम् ॥३१.६॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुः सेना॑यां॒ यां च॒क्रुरि॑ष्वायु॒धे। दु॑न्दु॒भौ कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in the army ( sénā ), what they have made in arrow-and-weapon; in the drum what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.
commentaries.whitney_notes: To make the meter complete in the two preceding verses, we need to make the unusual resolution -ya-am at end of a .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते चक्रुः सेनायां यां चक्रुरिष्वायुधे। दुन्दुभौ कृत्यां यां चक्रुः पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: याम् । ते । चक्रु: । सेनायाम् । याम् । चक्रु: । इषुआयुधे । दुन्दुभौ । कृत्याम् । याम् । चक्रु: । पुन: । प्रति । हरामि । ताम् ॥३१.७॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ कृ॒त्यां कूपे॑ऽवद॒धुः श्म॑शा॒ने वा॑ निच॒ख्नुः। सद्म॑नि कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुः पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What witchcraft they have put down for thee in the well, or have dug in at the cemetery; in the seat ( sádman ) what witchcraft they have made—I take that back again.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The indefinite 'seat' may be used for 'dwelling,' or for 'place of sacrifice.' The Anukr. takes no notice of the metrical irregularities in a, b .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते कृत्यां कूपेऽवदधुः श्मशाने वा निचख्नुः। सद्मनि कृत्यां यां चक्रुः पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: याम् । ते । कृत्याम् । कूपे । अवऽदधु: । श्मशाने । वा । निऽचख्नु: । सद्मनि । कृत्याम् । याम् । चक्रु: । पुन: । प्रति । हरामि । ताम् ॥३१.८॥

items.samhita_patha: यां ते॑ च॒क्रुः पु॑रुषा॒स्थे अ॒ग्नौ संक॑सुके च॒ याम्। म्रो॒कं नि॑र्दा॒हं क्र॒व्यादं॒ पुनः॒ प्रति॑ हरामि॒ ताम् ॥
items.pada_patha: याम् । ते॒ । च॒क्रु: । पु॒रु॒ष॒ऽअ॒स्ये । अ॒ग्नौ । सम्ऽक॑सुके । च॒ । याम् । भ्रो॒कम् । नि॒:ऽदा॒हम् । क्र॒व्य॒ऽअद॑म् ।पुन॑: । प्रति॑ । ह॒रा॒मि॒ । ताम् ॥३१.९॥

commentaries.whitney: What [witchcraft] they have made for thee in the human-bone, and what in the destroying (? sáṁkasuka ) fire, [what] dimming, out-burning, flesh-eating one—I take that back again.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Human-bone' (if not a corrupt reading) is perhaps an epithet of the funeral fire = 'the fire which leaves of the human body nothing but fragments of bone.'

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां ते चक्रुः पुरुषास्थे अग्नौ संकसुके च याम्। म्रोकं निर्दाहं क्रव्यादं पुनः प्रति हरामि ताम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: अप॑थे॒ना ज॑भारैणां॒ तां प॒थेतः प्र हि॑ण्मसि। अधी॑रो मर्या॒धीरे॑भ्यः॒ सं ज॑भा॒राचि॑त्त्या ॥

commentaries.whitney: He hath brought it by what was not the road; we send it forth from here by the road; he unwise, O men, hath brought [it] together, out of thoughtlessness, for the wise ( dhī́ra ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies the reading maryāḥ; dhī́rebhyaḥ: in c , instead of maryā॰dhī́rebhyaḥ , as given by the pada -mss.; the emendation is suggested by BR. v. 1668; but cf. maryādhāírya ( maryā [ ḥ ] dhāírya? ) in MS. i. 4. 8 (p. 56, 1. 18). The lingual ṇ in eṇām at end of a is given by all the saṁhitā -mss., though the Prāt. does not prescribe it. Even the pada -text has hiṇmasi (as hiṇmaḥ ) after pra , here as elsewhere.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अपथेना जभारैणां तां पथेतः प्र हिण्मसि। अधीरो मर्याधीरेभ्यः सं जभाराचित्त्या ॥

commentaries.whitney: He who hath made hath not been able to make; he hath crushed a foot, a finger; he, fortuneless, hath made what is excellent for us [who are] fortunate ones.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first three pādas are identical with iv. 18. 6 a-c , and our d here is read by Ppp. in that hymn ⌊but with abhagā for -gó ⌋. The Anukr. gives the same false definition of meter in both places. ⌊See notes to iv. 18. 6.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: यश्चकार न शशाक कर्तुं शश्रे पादमङ्गुरिम्। चकार भद्रमस्मभ्यमभगो भगवद्भ्यः ॥

items.samhita_patha: कृ॑त्या॒कृतं वल॒गिनं॑ मू॒लिनं॑ शपथे॒य्य॑म्। इन्द्र॒स्तं ह॑न्तु मह॒ता व॒धेना॒ग्निर्वि॑ध्यत्व॒स्तया॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: The witchcraft-maker, spell-hider, root-possessor, worthy of cursing—let Indra smite him with his great deadly weapon; let Agni pierce him with a hurled [arrow].
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse is found in Ppp. i., where, for c, d , is read: indras tu sarvāṅs tāṅ hantu sattvaghnena bhavām iva . The last or sixth anuvāka contains 5 hymns and 70 verses; the old Anukr. says: ṣaṣṭhe tu navāi ’kā ca parā tu ṣaṣṭhe . One or two of the mss. sum up the Book correctly as 31 hymns, and 376 verses. With the Book ends also the twelfth prapāṭhaka .
